script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'acquisitions-canada-search',
  description: 'Parallel Canadian (ON/BC) acquisition search up to ~$500K CAD; real deals per category + BDC/CSBFP financing + remote-operability-from-US flags, then a head-to-head',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Categories', detail: 'one agent per business category: real current Canadian listings, economics, Canadian financing, remote-operability' },
    { title: 'Synthesize', detail: 'head-to-head; best Canadian deals + how CA financing/immigration changes the picture vs the US search' },
  ],
}

const ROOT = '/home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research'
const OUT = `${ROOT}/acquisitions_canada`

const CATEGORIES = [
  { key: 'saas_software', name: 'SaaS / software / apps (Canadian-domiciled)',
    detail: 'Canadian-based vertical B2B SaaS, micro-SaaS, software/data products up to ~$500K CAD. Naturally remote-operable. Acquire.com/Flippa/EmpireFlippers (filter Canada), plus Canadian brokers.' },
  { key: 'ecommerce_brands', name: 'E-commerce / DTC brands (Canadian)',
    detail: 'Canadian DTC/e-commerce brands with a moat (brand/IP/repeat), not commodity dropshipping. Often remote-runnable. businessesforsale.com/canada, Flippa, Canadian brokers.' },
  { key: 'content_media', name: 'Content / media / newsletters / communities (Canadian)',
    detail: 'Canadian content/media/community assets with durable first-party audiences. Remote-runnable. Note AI-Overview/SEO risk.' },
  { key: 'local_service', name: 'Local service businesses (ON/BC home & trades)',
    detail: 'ON/BC home services & trades: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, landscaping, cleaning, pest, pool, restoration, junk removal. Recurring/route preferred. NOTE trade-licensing rules differ by province. Requires on-the-ground presence — flag this. Sunbelt Canada, businessesforsale.com/canada, BizBuySell Canada.' },
  { key: 'physical_asset', name: 'Physical / real-asset businesses (ON/BC, semi-absentee)',
    detail: 'ON/BC laundromats, self-storage, car washes, vending routes. Asset-backed, financeable via BDC/bank, manager/attendant-run. Some semi-absentee. Sunbelt Canada, Canadian brokers.' },
  { key: 'b2b_distribution', name: 'B2B distribution / niche manufacturing / light industrial (ON/BC)',
    detail: 'ON/BC small manufacturers, specialty distributors, B2B/commercial services. Real cash flow, seller financing + BDC common. Sunbelt Canada, businessesforsale.com/canada.' },
]

const CAT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['category','deals','category_economics','financing_notes','remote_operability','hooman_fit','category_verdict'],
  properties: {
    category: { type: 'string' },
    deals: {
      type: 'array', description: 'REAL current Canadian listings (do not invent); best-fit first',
      items: {
        type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['name','niche_location','asking_price','revenue','sde_cashflow','multiple','age','why_notable','risks','remote_runnable','fits_500k_cad'],
        properties: {
          name: { type: 'string' },
          niche_location: { type: 'string', description: 'niche + province/city' },
          asking_price: { type: 'string', description: 'CAD (note if USD)' },
          revenue: { type: 'string' },
          sde_cashflow: { type: 'string' },
          multiple: { type: 'string' },
          age: { type: 'string' },
          why_notable: { type: 'string' },
          risks: { type: 'string' },
          remote_runnable: { type: 'string', enum: ['REMOTE','SEMI-ABSENTEE','ON-SITE-REQUIRED'] },
          fits_500k_cad: { type: 'string', enum: ['FITS-ALL-CASH','FITS-WITH-FINANCING','OVER-500K'] },
        },
      },
    },
    category_economics: { type: 'string', description: 'typical Canadian SDE multiples, cash yields, owner-hours in this category' },
    financing_notes: { type: 'string', description: 'BDC / CSBFP / Canadian bank acquisition-financing feasibility for this category; typical down %; seller-note norms' },
    remote_operability: { type: 'string', description: 'can these be run remotely from the US (until/unless he relocates to Canada)?' },
    hooman_fit: { type: 'string' },
    category_verdict: { type: 'string' },
  },
}

phase('Categories')

const results = await parallel(CATEGORIES.map(c => () =>
  agent(
    `You are sourcing the BEST business ACQUISITIONS in CANADA (focus Ontario & British Columbia; note standout deals ` +
    `in other provinces) for Hooman. This is the CANADIAN parallel to a US search — keep it Canada-specific.\n` +
    `Constraints: up to ~$500K CAD of his own cash; time relaxed (willing to work harder / eventually leave his day ` +
    `job); ANY business type; goal = the best acquisition available.\n\n` +
    `FOUNDER: Canadian citizen, AI/ML + data engineering + cloud/infra + EE, strong diligence. CRITICAL CONTEXT: he ` +
    `is a Canadian citizen (so **Canadian financing — BDC, CSBFP, bank acquisition loans — IS available to him**, ` +
    `unlike US SBA). He CURRENTLY LIVES/WORKS IN THE US (TN visa, green card soon), so for each deal FLAG whether it ` +
    `can be run REMOTELY from the US, is SEMI-ABSENTEE, or REQUIRES on-the-ground presence in Canada — this is a real ` +
    `near-term constraint until/unless he relocates.\n\n` +
    `YOUR CATEGORY: ${c.name}\n  Scope: ${c.detail}\n\n` +
    `Read ${OUT}/README.md for the mandate. Do REAL WEB RESEARCH (WebSearch/WebFetch): browse actual Canadian ` +
    `marketplaces/brokers — businessesforsale.com/canada, Sunbelt Canada, BizBuySell (Canada filter), Acquire.com/` +
    `Flippa/EmpireFlippers (Canada), Kijiji/Spergel/DealStream, provincial business-broker sites. Capture REAL current ` +
    `listings with real numbers (asking in CAD, revenue, SDE/cash flow, multiple, age, city/province). Do NOT invent ` +
    `listings; mark gated fields "gated". Prioritize deals fitting ~$500K CAD (all-cash or BDC/seller-financed) with ` +
    `durable cash flow.\n\n` +
    `WRITE findings to ${OUT}/categories/${c.key}.md (use Write; create folders; include URLs where public; cite ` +
    `sources). THEN return the schema. Be honest and quantified; give the real Canadian economics and an honest ` +
    `verdict. Note Canadian specifics: provincial trade-licensing, HST, CAD pricing, and BDC/CSBFP down-payment norms.`,
    { label: `ca:${c.key}`, phase: 'Categories', schema: CAT_SCHEMA, agentType: 'general-purpose' }
  ).then(r => r ? { ...r, key: c.key } : null)
))

const cats = results.filter(Boolean)
const allDeals = cats.flatMap(c => (c.deals || []).map(d => ({ ...d, category: c.category })))
log(`Canadian category scan done: ${cats.length}/${CATEGORIES.length} categories, ${allDeals.length} real deals.`)

phase('Synthesize')

const digest = JSON.stringify({
  categories: cats.map(c => ({ category: c.category, economics: c.category_economics, financing: c.financing_notes, remote: c.remote_operability, fit: c.hooman_fit, verdict: c.category_verdict, deal_count: (c.deals||[]).length })),
  deals: allDeals,
}, null, 2)

const synthesis = await agent(
  `Produce a HEAD-TO-HEAD for the best CANADIAN (ON/BC) acquisition for Hooman at up to ~$500K CAD. He is a Canadian ` +
  `citizen (so BDC/CSBFP/bank financing IS available — unlike US SBA), currently living in the US on TN (green card ` +
  `soon), willing to go full-time. Skills: AI/ML, data eng, cloud/infra, EE, strong diligence.\n\n` +
  `All categories + real Canadian deals (JSON):\n${digest}\n\n` +
  `Read ${OUT}/README.md. Also read ${ROOT}/acquisitions_500k/WIDE_SEARCH_REPORT.md so you can DIRECTLY COMPARE the ` +
  `Canadian option to the US option.\n\n` +
  `WRITE ${OUT}/CANADA_SEARCH_REPORT.md with:\n` +
  `  1. Executive summary: the 3-5 best Canadian acquisitions, with the single top pick.\n` +
  `  2. Master ranked table of the best real Canadian deals (name, category, province, asking CAD, SDE, multiple, ` +
  `cash yield, remote-runnable?, Hooman-fit, financing, fits-$500K-CAD).\n` +
  `  3. Category heat-map for Canada.\n` +
  `  4. THE KEY COMPARISON: Canada vs US for this buyer. Canadian financing (BDC/CSBFP: typical down %, terms) + no ` +
  `visa issue, VS the US path once his green card lands (SBA leverage). Which unlocks a bigger/better business for ` +
  `his $500K? Factor in that he lives in the US now (remote-operability matters) and a green card is coming.\n` +
  `  5. Top 3-5 picks: honest cash flow, risks, owner-hours, remote-operability, where his edge is real.\n` +
  `  6. Bottom line: is the best Canadian deal better than the best US deal for him, considering financing, ` +
  `immigration, remote-operability, and the imminent green card? Give a clear recommendation.\n\n` +
  `Be concrete, quantified, skeptical. Return a ~450-word executive summary as your final text (relayed to Hooman).`,
  { label: 'canada-synthesis', phase: 'Synthesize', agentType: 'general-purpose' }
)

return {
  categories_scanned: cats.length,
  total_deals: allDeals.length,
  best_by_category: cats.map(c => ({ category: c.category, verdict: c.category_verdict })),
  synthesis_summary: synthesis,
}

best_by_category.verdict: STRONG BUY category — the best-fit and most remote-operable of the whole Canadian search — but the true sub-$500K all-cash shelf is thin. The genuinely durable, cash-flowing Canadian SaaS (BizQuest 16-yr BC staffing platform: <2% churn, 55% margin, ~4x SDE, ~$338K CAD SDE) sits at ~$1.35M CAD and is a finance-with-BDC/seller-note deal, not all-cash; the all-cash ≤$500K tier is dominated by 2026 'AI app' flips with no moat (skip). Recommended play: target one proven, low-churn vertical B2B SaaS in the $700K–$1.35M range, put ~$400–500K CAD down, and lever the rest with BDC + seller paper — using Canadian citizenship for the financing he can't get in the US. Lead candidate: #1 BC Staffing-Mgmt SaaS; watch #2 Quebec SaaS (if near $500K) and #4 Ontario cybersecurity SaaS (if priced modestly) as closer-to-all-cash alternatives. Note: Flippa/Acquire.com/DealStream detail pages were 403/JS-blocked via WebFetch — a manual browser pass is needed to fully sweep the true ≤$500K all-cash micro-SaaS band.

MODERATE — cautiously positive but not the top category for this founder. Canadian sub-$500K DTC brands exist, are cheap (2.5-4x SDE), and several offer seller financing; a couple are genuinely good businesses. Standout best-fit-for-budget: the Central-Ontario natural-deodorant brand ($349K / $100K SDE, 13 yrs, 1,000+ Amazon Subscribe & Save recurring, retirement seller, seller financing, all-cash-affordable) — buy it with a contract co-packer + 3PL installed so it runs semi-absentee while Hooman is US-based. Caveats dragging the category down: (1) the moat is a physical consumable, so it's semi-absentee at best from the US, not remote; (2) the category barely uses Hooman's AI/data edge; (3) CSBFP won't finance goodwill and BDC discounts it, so leverage is limited — mostly cash+seller-note deals; (4) inventory-bundled pricing and gated financials demand heavy diligence. The Smart-Home SaaS+e-com is the only truly-remote/founder-fit option but is a turnaround. Note: businessesforsale.com/canada, Flippa, Empire Flippers and Acquire.com block automated scraping and hide seller location pre-account, so additional Canadian FBA/DTC inventory almost certainly exists there and warrants a manual/account-based pass.

WEAK-to-MODERATE fit; do not prioritize as the primary acquisition. The Canadian content/media market at <=$500K CAD is dominated by declining print, on-site creative-service agencies, and franchise photography - none durable, remote, and founder-fit. The genuinely attractive profile (durable first-party audience, remote, high margin) is rare; the one strong example, the Vancouver Clean Energy Media Platform, is ~$2.4M at ~10x EBITDA, revenue-lumpy, vertically concentrated, and goodwill-only (hard for BDC to lever, a stretch even with heavy seller financing on $500K cash). Content assets are also the most exposed to AI-Overview/SEO decay and least aligned with the Canadian-domicile financing/immigration thesis. If pursued anyway: (1) negotiate the Vancouver platform down with a heavy seller note and add AI/data products where Hooman's skills create value, or (2) buy a smaller $100-300K content/newsletter asset off Flippa/Acquire as a cash-flowing secondary, accepting it likely won't be Canadian-domiciled. Otherwise route the primary $500K to a category with hard cash flow BDC will lever and clearer founder-fit.

MEDIOCRE FIT — not recommended as the #1 acquisition while Hooman lives in the US. Economics are attractive (2-3x SDE, 30-40% unlevered yields, BDC/VTB financing genuinely available to a Canadian citizen), but every deal is physically on-the-ground and most trades require a license Hooman doesn't hold, so he'd be an absentee cross-border owner on day one — the worst posture for a hands-on service business. If pursued anyway, ranked shortlist: (1) Richmond low-voltage integrator $389K — best founder-fit (EE/AI adjacency, existing AI automation), retained team, 20-30% down seller financing, semi-absentee-plausible; diligence the technical-lead key-man risk and verify $130K SDE. (2) CertaPro painting franchise St. Catharines $385K (~2.1x SDE) — crew-manage model, franchisor scaffolding. (3) Toronto fence $559K — only if diligence explains the ~1.5x SDE and the 11% margin isn't a mirage. Treat this whole category as a RELOCATION-CONTINGENT option; revisit seriously once Hooman is in Canada. Until then favour remote-runnable software/SaaS acquisitions.

best_by_category.category: Physical / real-asset businesses (ON/BC): laundromats, self-storage, car washes, vending routes
best_by_category.verdict: Asset-backed and financeable, but a weak founder-fit and weak remote-fit for Hooman right now. Deals that fit $500K all-cash (leasehold laundromats, self-serve car-wash leaseholds, vending) are low-SDE, financially opaque, utility-inflation-exposed, and mostly require local presence — the exact constraints that hurt a US-resident AI/data engineer most. The genuinely attractive assets (express car washes, self-storage) have great low-labor cash flow but sit at $1.5M-$10M and need real leverage plus relocation or a hired operator. Recommended shape if pursued: (1) best all-cash pick = a metro unattended, card/app-enabled laundromat with a long lease priced ≤$450K, where his tech edge and the only real remote-operability live — diligence must VERIFY coin/app revenue and lease term; (2) best leverage pick = a car-wash/small-storage WITH real estate (~$1.2-1.6M) using $400-500K down + BDC/commercial mortgage, trading remote-operability for a better appreciating asset. Overall: worth one serious laundromat swing, but this category ranks BELOW the software/online acquisition categories for a remote US-based AI founder.

best_by_category.category: B2B distribution / niche manufacturing / light industrial (ON & BC)
best_by_category.verdict: Weak-to-moderate fit for THIS founder — pursue only one specific deal, and only if relocating. The category delivers exactly what it promises: real, durable, AI-safe cash flow at honest (often cheap) 2–3x SDE multiples. The two genuinely good businesses are the BC General Contractor (#44625001, $495K / ~$235K SDE / 2.1x / seller-financed, fits all-cash) and the Toronto HVAC contractor (#45025001, $1.1M / ~$391K SDE / 2.8x, partly recurring, financeable). But the category collides head-on with Hooman's two hard constraints: he lives in the US and can't be on-site, and the cash flow is owner-labour + trade-license-gated rather than software-scalable, so his edge is wasted and he'd buy a GM's salary out of the returns. If he intends to relocate to Canada and wants boring, steady cash flow, diligence the HVAC (best multiple on real, partly-recurring SDE) or the BC GC (cheapest, seller-financed, but essentially a job). As a REMOTE secondary income while still in the US, this category is not the answer — a manager-run distributor is the only shape that could work, and none in-budget here have disclosed financials to justify it. Weigh against software/SaaS categories where his edge and remote constraint actually align. Sourcing caveat: BizBuySell, businessesforsale.com, Sunbelt Canada and DealStream all blocked automated fetch; verified listings above came from BusinessSellCanada.com — broader marketplaces likely hold more inventory in this category.

# Executive Summary — Best Canadian Acquisition for Hooman

Scored on cash yield, multiple fairness, durability, owner-dependence, founder-fit, remote-operability-from-US, and BDC/CSBFP financing feasibility. The binding Canadian constraint is remote-operability while he still lives in the US — which structurally favors software.

**Top pick — BC Staffing-Management Vertical SaaS (~$1.35M CAD; finance with BDC + seller note).** 16-yr B2B SaaS, US$249K SDE (~$338K CAD, 55% margin), 100+ clients, 90%+ recurring, <2% churn, 32% YoY growth, runs on 5 home-based contractors. It's the single most remote-operable and highest-founder-fit asset in the whole Canadian search — runnable from the US on TN today, and his exact skillset (modernize the 16-yr codebase, cut infra cost, add AI). USD-priced (>$1M CAD), so it's a ~$400–500K CAD down + BDC term loan + seller-note deal — precisely the leverage his citizenship unlocks. Biggest risk: growth is owner-led outbound/conference sales he must replace.

**Runners-up:** #2 Richmond BC Low-Voltage Integrator ($389K / $130K SDE / ~3.0x, all-cash) — an EE/electronics business already doing "AI proposal automation," retained team, 20–30% down VTB, best all-cash operating fit. #3 Central-ON Natural Deodorant DTC ($349K / $100K SDE, all-cash, seller financing) — cleanest cash-flowing brand but semi-absentee only with a co-packer/3PL and underuses his edge. #4 Ontario Cybersecurity SaaS (CA$207K rev, gated) — fully remote, compliance-driven, strong fit if repriced.

**The key Canada-vs-US finding:** The US report's premise ("no-SBA = 3–4x smaller business") is a US-*asset* problem, not a Canadian-*buyer* problem. As a Canadian citizen, **BDC substitutes cleanly for SBA — ~25% down reaches a ~$1.3–2M business, roughly matching the US SBA path (~10% down → $1–2M).** So leverage size is a wash. The decisive differences are **timing and remote-operability**: Canada works *today* with no visa issue, letting him own AND operate a Canadian company remotely from the US on TN; the US SBA path is locked until the green card lands. The green card is a future option that, at best, *matches* the leverage he already has in Canada — it doesn't produce a better asset than a remote Canadian SaaS he can start compounding now.

**Bottom line:** The best Canadian deal is better for him right now, and the imminent green card doesn't change that. Recommendation: pursue the **BC Staffing SaaS** (BDC + seller note, BC-incorporated, run remotely; diligence sales dependence hardest); all-cash alternatives are the **Richmond Low-Voltage Integrator** or a repriced **Ontario Cybersecurity SaaS**. Deprioritize Canadian trades/physical/manufacturing while US-resident — cheap and BDC-leverageable but on-site and license-gated (relocation-contingent). Caveat: Flippa/Acquire/DealStream pages were blocked; a manual pass is needed to fully sweep the ≤$500K all-cash micro-SaaS band.
